# Better design before analysis. Better evidence after it.

SomaSens is a growing collection of practical notes for designing SomaScan
studies, recognizing unwanted variation, and making defensible analysis
decisions.

[Explore pre-analytical variation](scripts/index.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-lg}
[Plan plate randomization](randomization.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary .btn-lg}
:::

## Why this matters

SomaScan measurements can be sensitive to what happens before the assay,
including fed-versus-fasted state, freeze-thaw history, hemolysis, and delays
between collection, processing, and freezing
[@han2021nutrient; @candia2025hemolysis; @tatsumi2026preanalytical]. If these
factors differ systematically between study groups, they can create broad
protein shifts, unexplained sample clusters, or misleading associations.

Known processing-sensitive protein signatures can sometimes help diagnose the
source of a problem. The current detailed report shows how to compare an
observed between-group signal with those signatures and how to calculate a
sample-level fed-fasted score.

::: {.takeaway}
### The practical conclusion

Diagnosis does not guarantee that the affected measurements can be repaired.
When a processing effect is large, excluding a clearly defined set of affected
samples may be more defensible than relying on statistical adjustment alone,
although filtering also reduces power and can introduce selection bias. The
best protection is consistent sample preparation, balanced study design, and a
complete record of what happened to every sample.
:::

## A simple working principle

::: {.principle-row}
::: {.principle-step}
<span class="step-number">1</span>

**Prevent**

Standardize collection and processing wherever possible.
:::

::: {.principle-step}
<span class="step-number">2</span>

**Record**

Keep sample-level times, handling events, storage history, plate, and well.
:::

::: {.principle-step}
<span class="step-number">3</span>

**Balance**

Distribute biological groups across plates and available well positions.
:::

::: {.principle-step}
<span class="step-number">4</span>

**Diagnose**

Inspect structure before testing the primary biological hypothesis.
:::
:::
